workload: Repeated cue-and-commit T-maze with a hidden left/right reward context
environment: Every trial starts at the same junction, supplies one left/right cue, and ends with one committed arm choice. A fresh trial begins on the next tick. Arm payoffs are recorded by the evaluator and withheld from both filters. There is no action-dependent observation channel, so the paired agents can share the exact observation tape.
generator: numpy.random.Generator(PCG64(seed)). Draw first context with integers(2); before each subsequent period flip context iff random()<0.20; for each child tick report the true side iff random()<0.72. The same cues go to both controllers.
emission: Identity from child cue state to observed side. Each parent regime selects a two-state child transition with equal columns and the prescribed cue accuracy.
policy: Choose the arm with higher posterior expected reward, breaking ties to the lowest index. Score every real trial. The flat agent has the same one-trial mixture, preferences and observation but marginalizes the regime independently at each new trial. Separately report a flat HMM with per-tick switch probability 0.20/8, which retains history and has no explicit period boundaries.
primary_parent_metric: Mean posterior mass assigned to the true regime at the final child tick of each parent period; threshold >=0.75.
primary_task_metric: Across all matched trials the hierarchical success rate exceeds the independent-trial flat baseline by at least 0.06 in absolute success probability. Report each seed and the history-using flat control. No threshold is imposed against the history-using control.
verification: Record action, status, posterior, cue and true side by seed and tick, full configuration, source revision, and a digest of the serialized hierarchy; retain all invalid statuses and do not rank an incomplete cohort. Check parent beliefs versus an independent float64 forward recurrence. The tiny exact ledger and hostile-input tests are separate from this controlled behavioral outcome.
